props.name: mixed contact masses of non-reducible oxides of metals of different periodic groups, more basic oxide preponderating
props.description: Contact masses containing mixtures of oxides of metals of different groups of the periodic system that are not reduced to the metals under the working conditions, with the more basic oxide in preponderating quantity; non-reducible oxides of the second to seventh groups especially suitable.

evidence.quote: the aforementioned process can be carried out with particular advantage by using contact masses containing mixtures of such oxids of metals of different groups of the periodic system as are not reduced to the metals under the conditions of working
and with a preponderating quantity of the more basic oxid. Non-reducible oxids of the second to the seventh group of the periodic System are especially suitable for such mixed cata lysts.

props.name: zinc oxide-chromium oxide contact mass, zinc oxide preponderating (2 to 12 or more mol ZnO per mol chromium oxide)

evidence.quote: As an example we mention the combina tion of zinc oxid and chromium oxid with the zinc oxid preponderating; from two to twelve or more mol. weights of zinc oxid may be present for each one molecular weight of chromium oxid.

props.statement: It is advisable to keep the contact masses free from iron and nickel (or allow only comparatively small amounts), to keep the reaction gas free from volatile iron and nickel compounds, and to build the apparatus so that the contact mass is not contaminated by iron, e.g. making it from copper or lining it inside with copper.

props.name: preparation of the mixed contact masses

evidence.quote: The mixed contact masses of the charac ter described may be prepared by intimately mixing the constituents, or by simultane ously precipitating them from solutions of proper salts, or by melting suitable salts together, or in any other suitable way.
Supports may also be employed.

props.name: reduction of carbon monoxide or dioxide with hydrogen to methanol or other oxygenated organic compounds
props.description: The process as the patent names it: carbon monoxide or dioxide reduced with hydrogen at elevated temperature and pressure to methanol or other oxygenated organic compounds.

evidence.quote: By the reduction of carbon monoxid or dioxid with hydrogen at an elevated ten perature and pressure methanol or other oxygenated organic compounds can be pro duced, provided proper catalysts are used.
